title: Edge routing, done the practical way
summary: Adtran’s cost-effective edge router solution extends 400G to the network edge, enabling a Terabit-scale edge solution without the space, power and cost overheads often tied to traditional platforms.
body_text: Why the network edge needs 400G today Traffic at the network edge is growing fast, and many existing networks weren’t built to handle it efficiently. Where access networks like fiber broadband and mobile backhaul connect to aggregation and core networks, this challenge is especially noticeable. As traffic grows, simply adding more 100Gbit/s interfaces increases space, power consumption and operational complexity, making traditional scaling models inefficient and costly. “Modern” routers haven’t really changed that equation. They’re often expensive, power-hungry and just all around large , which adds cost and complexity even when they’re marketed as next-generation platforms. At Adtran, we’re applying real-world experience to the next generation of edge routing. Building on proven 100Gbit/s edge router deployments, including work with the Telecom Infra Project, our edge router solution introduces 400Gbit/s-enabled interfaces at the network edge, delivering high capacity while reducing space and power requirements compared to traditional designs. It provides high-capacity routing without the cost or power draw of older, oversized systems. With integrated MPLS routing, coherent optics and a common software foundation for automation , Adtran enables long-term growth while keeping the network flexible, efficient and future-ready, supporting a clear path to Terabit-scale edge capacity as demand continues to grow. Cost-effective 400G edge routing at scale When it comes to edge networking, performance doesn’t have to come at a premium. While many vendors now offer 400Gbit/s-capable edge platforms, solutions can cost over $100K per unit , often before software is included, with comparable capabilities to Adtran’s edge routers. In contrast, Adtran’s edge routers deliver reliable high-capacity routing with 400Gbit/s interfaces at a fraction of the cost . The solution spans compact, cabinet-ready platforms for space-constrained edge deployments as well as high-density systems designed for large-scale aggregation environments, ensuring the right fit across different edge scenarios. Adtran’s high-density, low-cost platforms make it easier to add capacity without introducing expensive hardware or complex integrations. Edge aggregation doesn’t have to be expensive – our solution makes scaling both affordable and simple. Seamless scalability from 10G to 400G From 5G backhaul to fiber broadband aggregation, Adtran’s edge router solution is built to scale as traffic increases. With native support for 10, 100 and 400Gbit/s speeds , our routers allow networks to scale without disruptive hardware upgrades. Built-in automation with Adtran’s carrier-grade network operating system (NOS) provides a consistent software foundation across edge routing platforms. This simplifies provisioning and management as networks scale. By decoupling software from hardware, the solution allows operators to deploy, expand and evolve edge routing platforms without changing their operational model. Whether you’re handling growing traffic volumes or deploying new services, Adtran’s solution provides the flexibility and scalability you need to stay ahead of future demands, without costly upgrades or downtime. This future-proof design saves you from the need for frequent, expensive hardware refreshes. Simplified edge architecture with integrated routing and coherent optics Adtran’s edge router solution, with 400Gbit/s interfaces, is designed to simplify your network by seamlessly integrating routing capabilities with coherent optics. With plug-and-play integration of ZR/ZR+ coherent optics , our routers enable high-capacity 400Gbit/s connections directly from the router. This easy integration supports seamless scaling of your network to 400Gbit/s speeds, while maintaining compatibility with modern MPLS traffic management. Integrated coherent optics, combined with optional IP OLS capabilities, extends the reach of 400Gbit/s traffic and enables high-capacity packet edge transport, amplifying signals to 120km+ . This approach enhances the routing platform without introducing additional complexity, making it easier to scale without adding unnecessary equipment. As your network needs grow, the IP OLS system can scale to 800Gbit/s, allowing the network to scale easily when you’re ready. The modular nature of our solution means you can add only the components you need, avoiding unnecessary complexity and keeping your network efficient and adaptable. Why Adtran leads in cost-effective 400G edge routing High-capacity hardware alone doesn’t solve the challenges of scaling the network edge. Throughout this blog, we’ve talked about cost-effective hardware, seamless scalability and simplified integration. What makes those advantages practical at scale is a combination of high-capacity hardware, integrated optics and a consistent software foundation that simplifies operations as networks grow. A consistent software foundation across the edge : Delivers a unified feature set, command structure and automation framework across deployments, reducing operational complexity as networks scale from 10Gbit/s to 400Gbit/s. Automation that makes 400Gbit/s practical : Simplifies provisioning, configuration and lifecycle management, reducing cost and enabling service providers to deploy high-capacity routing without adding complexity Hardware flexibility without lock-in : Allows independent evolution of software and hardware, empowering operators to deploy, expand and refresh edge routing platforms without changing their operational model. Integrated routing and optics : Combines plug-and-play coherent optics and IP OLS capabilities within the routing architecture to simplify network design with fewer devices and fewer failure points. A complete ecosystem : Adtran delivers an end-to-end portfolio of hardware, software and services, simplifying operations from access to core. Ready to modernize your network edge with 400G? Outdated and expensive routers can quickly become a scaling barrier as edge traffic increases. Adtran’s edge router solution extends 400Gbit/s to the network edge with the performance, scalability and cost-effectiveness needed to stay ahead of growing demands. Whether you're upgrading for 5G, expanding your fiber broadband footprint, or preparing for future IoT demands, our solution is designed to scale with your business and simplify your network infrastructure. (“BUZZ HPC” or “BUZZ”), today announced that BUZZ is advancing a major infrastructure investment in Ontario, anchored by a planned new industrial-scale AI infrastructure facility, also known as an AI gigafactory, in the Greater Toronto Area (“GTA”) with approximately 320 megawatts (“MW”) of utility capacity. The project is expected to become one of Canada’s largest AI gigafactories, designed to support fully vertically integrated AI supercomputers and host more than 100,000 GPUs at full build-out. An AI gigafactory is the industrial infrastructure of the intelligence economy: a facility that converts compute into intelligence, helping make Canadian businesses more competitive. Canada Invented Modern AI. Now It Is Building the Factories That Will Own It. BUZZ High Performance Computing Inc. acquired land comprising approximately 21 acres (the “Main Parcel”) for a purchase price of $46 million, as well as an additional parcel of land adjacent to the Main Parcel, measuring approximately 4 acres (the “Additional Parcel”), for a purchase price of $12 million. The Main Parcel and the Additional Parcel collectively comprise a contiguous site benefiting from a 320 MW power allocation. BUZZ has secured major milestones along the project’s 320 MW power pathway to develop sovereign AI infrastructure in the Toronto–Waterloo innovation corridor. The project is designed to place massive industrial-scale compute directly inside Canada’s largest metropolitan economy and one of North America’s most important hubs for technology, financial services, and artificial intelligence. The vision of sovereign AI infrastructure is to provide the physical backbone for Canada’s intelligence economy. Compute is the new sovereignty. Countries that own the machines will write the future. Countries that rent compute from data centers abroad will not contain sensitive data within their borders. Located within one of the most important 100-kilometre corridors in global AI, the project is positioned between Geoffrey Hinton’s legacy, the University of Toronto and the Vector Institute to the east, and Waterloo’s world-leading systems and engineering talent to the west. This places the facility at the intersection of research excellence, enterprise demand, and low-latency global network connectivity. Key Highlights: Target Online: Second half of 2027. Capital Investment: ~CAD $3.5 billion. Jobs: 800+ construction, hundreds of permanent high-skill roles. Powered by Ontario’s Clean Grid: Designed for high efficiency AI compute using closed-loop cooling systems with no-water use approach consistent with BUZZ HPC’s broader sustainability strategy. Community First Approach : Focused on responsible development, local economic participation and long-term alignment with national priorities. Frank Holmes, Executive Chairman of HIVE and BUZZ: “AI is the new industrial base and compute is the factory floor. Canada produced the Godfathers of deep learning but kept renting the factories. That era is over. Between Toronto and Waterloo, BUZZ is building the sovereign AI infrastructure that turns Canadian intelligence into Canadian dominance. At full build-out, this intelligence factory will deploy over 100,000 GPUs, creating one of North America’s largest domestically controlled AI clusters. Low-latency inference, AI agents, financial platforms, healthcare breakthroughs, scientific discovery, and national priority workloads will finally run on Canadian iron, under Canadian control. Our vision is to build AI infrastructure that will serve humanity, with the potential to improve quality of life for millions of Canadians.” Aydin Kilic, President & CEO of HIVE Digital Technologies: “We have been strategically land-banking by regional substations, and we are very pleased to announce this expansion. HIVE now has over 850 MW of power globally; this includes our 450 MW of operating data centers plus a pipeline of 400 MW of capacity, which we expect to bring online in 2027. Globally diversified growth, this includes our 100 MW of operating data centers in Canada, now with a pipeline of 320 MW for 2027. BUZZ has done a phenomenal job expanding our footprint in Canada. With 5,500 GPUs online today doing AI compute, along with our 70 MW New Brunswick Grand Falls site, and now our 320 MW GTA site, we have the land and power to develop a pipeline of infrastructure to support approximately 130,000 GPUs. This puts HIVE and BUZZ at a global scale, with the largest AI native clouds.” Craig Tavares, President & COO of BUZZ HPC: “This investment is nationally important to Canada’s efforts to build the infrastructure required for the next generation of AI innovation. Compute is the new engine of the AI economy. If Canada wants to lead in AI, we need to build the factories that produce intelligence here at home. Canada has the clean energy, network connectivity and research ecosystem to lead AI innovation around the world. BUZZ is building the infrastructure layer that turns Canada’s AI ambition into reality. This gigafactory is the engine Canada needs to lead the intelligence economy. This facility anchors BUZZ’s national AI platform spanning British Columbia, Manitoba, Ontario, Quebec, and New Brunswick. It is being built as a fully vertically integrated, Canadian-governed supercomputing platform for the age of inference and enterprise AI. Being a Greater Toronto Area resident, it is an honor to build Canada’s first AI gigafactory in our community. I believe the jobs and economic development this project will offer, will provide tremendous value to the community.” About HIVE Digital Technologies Ltd. Today, HIVE builds and operates next-generation Tier-I and Tier-III data centers across Canada, Sweden, and Paraguay, serving both Bitcoin and high-performance computing clients. Non-GAAP Financial Measures This news release contains discussions of consolidated segment profit (loss) and margin, adjusted net earnings (loss), adjusted EPS and adjusted EBITDA that are non-GAAP financial measures under SEC rules. Segment profit (loss) is calculated as revenue less cost of revenue and earnings attributable to noncontrolling interests. The company believes that segment profit (loss) provides a meaningful perspective on its business results as it is the aggregation of individual segment profit measures that the company utilizes to evaluate and manage its business performance. Adjusted net earnings (loss) is defined as net earnings (loss) from core operations excluding equity method earnings and the impacts of foreign exchange fluctuations, impairments and certain items that management believes are unrelated to actual normalized operational performance. Net earnings (loss) from core operations is net earnings (loss) attributable to Fluor excluding the results of our remaining Stork and AMECO equipment businesses that are no longer classified as discontinued operations but that continue to be marketed for sale or that have been sold. Adjusted EPS is defined as adjusted net earnings divided by weighted average diluted shares outstanding. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net earnings from operations before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA), further adjusted by the same items excluded from adjusted net earnings. The company believes adjusted net earnings, adjusted EPS and adjusted EBITDA allow investors to evaluate the company’s ongoing earnings on a normalized basis and make meaningful period-over-period comparisons. However, non-GAAP measures have limitations as analytical tools and should not be considered in isolation from or a substitute for measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP. In addition, these non-GAAP measures are not necessarily comparable to similarly titled measures reported by other companies. Reconciliations of consolidated segment profit (loss) adjusted net earnings, adjusted EPS and adjusted EBITDA to the most comparable GAAP measures are included in the press release tables. The company is unable to provide a reconciliation of its adjusted EPS and adjusted EBITDA guidance to the most comparable GAAP measure without unreasonable efforts because it is unable to predict with reasonable certainty all of the components required to provide such reconciliation, including the impact of foreign exchange fluctuations, which are uncertain and could have a material impact on GAAP reported results for the guidance period.
